findings.description: The policy grants ec2:*, s3:*, lambda:* and cloudwatch:* on Resource "*" with no conditions. This is full administrative control over four services including all S3 data, all EC2 instances, and the ability to create or modify Lambda functions, far exceeding what a deployment identity requires (least privilege violation).

Action "lambda:*" and "ec2:*" on "*" allow the principal to create Lambda functions or launch EC2 instances with an arbitrary IAM role, and to pass roles (iam:PassRole is implicit via the service actions) — a well-known escalation path from a low-privileged identity to full account compromise.

A static, non-rotating access key pair is provisioned for the IAM user; the secret has no expiration and is directly usable for programmatic access. Long-lived credentials bound to an over-permissive policy substantially widen the blast radius if leaked.

The access key material is exposed as a Terraform output, persisting the credential in state, plan files and CI logs. Note the reference uses the non-existent attribute encrypted_secret, which would fail to evaluate, but the intent is to emit secret material which is itself the exposure.
The IAM user has no MFA device attached and no policy requiring MFA for the API actions it is granted. If the credentials are stolen they can be used without a second factor.
The user is created without a permissions boundary, so there is no upper bound capping the effective permissions granted by attached or inline policies.
